definition: Inquisitor means a person who questions others aggressively or in a hostile, relentless manner.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word inquisitor. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know inquisitor should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: By the third round of rapid-fire questions about her weekend, Dana told her roommate to stop playing inquisitor.
A questioner simply wants information, while an inquisitor hammers at you as if you were on trial.
An interrogator questions you intensely and officially, but an inquisitor adds a relentless, accusing zeal.

A cross-examiner tests testimony in court, probing sharply but within legal rules and limits. An inquisitor recognizes no such limits: the questioning is hostile and accusing wherever it happens, courtroom or kitchen. A cross-examiner's sharpness serves procedure; an inquisitor's serves zeal.

An examiner is a neutral person who tests or inspects — grading papers, checking eyesight — with no hostility implied at all. An inquisitor is never neutral: the word accuses someone of grilling with hostile, relentless persistence. Examiners assess; inquisitors accuse.

A prosecutor is a courtroom official whose job is to accuse and argue the case against a defendant, inside the law. An inquisitor may hold no office at all: the word names a manner — hostile, relentless questioning that presumes guilt. Prosecutor names a role; inquisitor names a style.
